html:
A marble column about 30 m high in Trajan's Forum in Rome, dedicated in 113 to mark the emperor Trajan's victories in Dacia. It was probably designed by Apollodorus of Damascus.

A carved band winds 23 times up the shaft and tells the story of the Dacian Wars of 101 to 102 and 105 to 106 in about 2,600 figures. Soldiers march, build camps and bridges, fight, and take prisoners; Trajan appears again and again. It is one of the best pictures we have of the Roman army at work, though the top scenes are hard to see from the ground.

Trajan's ashes were placed in the base. His bronze statue on top was lost and was replaced by one of Saint Peter in 1588. The column was copied by the Column of Marcus Aurelius and, much later, by victory columns in Paris and elsewhere.
sum: A marble column about 30 m high in Trajan's Forum in Rome, dedicated in 113 to mark the emperor Trajan's victories in Dacia. It was probably designed by Apollodorus of Damascus.
